title: PoE-Powered Ethernet Sensor Node
description: The split between what BRIEF.md fixes and what it leaves open. Every fixed_requirements entry carries the verbatim brief text that substantiates it, bound to the recorded brief digest. An open_decisions entry is a choice for the design agent: record it in 'chosen' with 'rationale', and never move it into fixed_requirements. Missing details are design freedom, not permission to fabricate unstated user requirements.

brief.authority: supplied by the benchmark; authoritative; preserved byte for byte and never edited

derivation.method: BRIEF.md was read and split; no design decision was taken. Every fixed_requirements entry, and every spec-table row sourced from the brief, carries a quotation that was checked by literal substring match against the brief bytes digested above. The build refuses to emit this file if any quotation is not found.
derivation.where_the_quotations_are: Every one of them is in this file: fixed_requirements[].brief_evidence and brief_spec_rows[].brief_evidence. The count above is the sum of those two lists, so it is recomputable from this repository alone - re-read BRIEF.md and check each string is a substring of it. brief_spec_rows carries the quotations behind the README's spec table, which would otherwise cite the brief with the evidence left in a build script.
derivation.review: two rounds of adversarial review against the brief, looking for invented requirements, lost requirements, evidence supporting a weaker claim than the one made beside it, and worksheet questions that presuppose their own answer

open_decisions.decision: PoE PD front-end implementation: how detection and classification signatures are formed, which 802.3af class is declared, whether an integrated PD controller or discrete arrangement is used, and how inrush and hot-swap are handled.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires a PoE PD interface and names IEEE 802.3af, but specifies no controller, no class, and no signature or inrush approach.

open_decisions.decision: Which PoE feed alternatives the node accepts — Alternative A, Alternative B, or both — and which pair-set polarities it accepts, and what circuitry at the input implements the behaviour chosen.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names 802.3af but says nothing about which alternatives or polarities the node must accept.

open_decisions.decision: Isolated converter design: controller, transformer, turns ratio, switching frequency, peak-current and duty limits, snubber/clamp, and rectification scheme.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires isolated DC/DC conversion and refers to flyback switching currents, but fixes no device, no magnetics and no operating point.

open_decisions.decision: Secondary-side rail voltages, currents and total power budget, and the load tally that justifies them.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no rail voltage, no current, and no power figure anywhere; the available budget must be derived from the standard and the design's own loads.

open_decisions.decision: Feedback and regulation path across the barrier: optocoupler, primary-side regulation, auxiliary winding, or a digital isolator, plus any additional isolated signal crossings.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief says the DC/DC is isolated but is silent on how regulation information crosses the barrier.

open_decisions.decision: Where the isolation barrier is drawn on the board, and which side the PHY, the MCU and the magnetics sit on.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief places the sensors on the isolated low-voltage side but does not state the domain of the PHY/MCU or where the barrier cuts the floorplan.

open_decisions.decision: Isolation target: working voltage, the safety or insulation standard being met, and the resulting creepage and clearance distances, keepout width and any slot/cutout.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires that isolation spacing be respected but names no voltage, no standard and no dimension.

open_decisions.decision: Magnetics arrangement: integrated magjack versus discrete magnetics with a separate RJ45, and how PoE power is tapped (centre-tap access, current rating, termination network).
open_decisions.why_open: The brief only requires an arrangement "appropriate to PoE" and names no part or configuration.

open_decisions.decision: Ethernet PHY selection, the MAC interface (and whether the MAC lives in the MCU or a separate device), reference-clock source and strapping/management interface.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names "Ethernet PHY/MCU" as a block with no device, interface or clocking specified.

open_decisions.decision: MCU selection: architecture, memory, package, peripheral set and how it is provisioned (MAC address, firmware, bootloader).
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names an MCU only as a block, with no family, vendor or capability stated.

open_decisions.decision: Sensor interface definition: how many connectors "several" means, connector type and pinout, the bus or signal type used, and whether sensor power is provided.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief gives a vague quantity and calls the sensors "low-speed" without naming a protocol, connector or count.

open_decisions.decision: Stackup and impedance: layer assignment, dielectric and copper thicknesses, reference planes, and the trace geometry that hits the 100BASE-TX differential target, plus whether controlled impedance is ordered.
open_decisions.why_open: Metadata gives 4 as a likely layer count only; the brief states no stackup, no dielectric and no impedance number.

open_decisions.decision: Grounding strategy: primary/secondary/chassis ground definitions, any Y-capacitor or stitching across the barrier, and how the shield and RJ45 termination network connect.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on grounding beyond requiring isolation spacing and noise separation.

open_decisions.decision: Transient protection strategy on the RJ45, the PoE input and the sensor connectors, and any surge or ESD level targeted.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief does not mention protection, ESD or surge at all; the exposure is inherent to a cable-connected PoE node, so the level and approach are the design's to set.

open_decisions.decision: Thermal design: dissipation budget and copper/airflow strategy for the PD hot-swap element, the converter switch and the magnetics, and the ambient assumed.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no ambient, enclosure, power dissipation or thermal requirement.

open_decisions.decision: EMC approach: common-mode chokes, filtering, switching-node containment and any conducted/radiated emissions target.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief flags flyback noise as a placement concern but sets no emissions target or filtering requirement.

open_decisions.decision: Board outline, dimensions, connector edge placement, mounting holes and any enclosure or panelization assumption.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no mechanical constraint of any kind.

open_decisions.decision: Test and bring-up provisions: debug/programming access, test points, link/status indication, and how the isolated side is exercised safely in production test.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief specifies no test, debug or indicator requirement.
